title: My 8-year-old directs Claude Code to make his Unity web game. Feedback welcome before he publishes it
author: YouCantGoThat_Way
selftext:
My son (8) is making Jurassic Rampage, a raptor-vs-zombies shooter. He plays each build and tells Claude Code what to change ("the helicopter flew through a house," "the zombies should actually bite the raptor," "that muzzle flash is terrible"). Claude writes all the C#. I watch and handle the deploys.  
  
It's Unity 6, built for WebGL and hosted on a Cloudflare Worker. Concept art came from ChatGPT, some models from Meshy and Tripo (the Brute boss is a Tripo model rigged in Mixamo), and some sounds from ElevenLabs. The zombies and guns are Unity Asset Store packs. Claude also writes its own checks, such as one that confirms every level has a route to the checkpoint, and screenshot modes so it can see what it built.  
  
He wants to publish on CrazyGames, and I'd like outside opinions first. Reply here and I'll pass along whatever's constructive.  
  
[https://jurassic-rampage.keleuo.com](https://jurassic-rampage.keleuo.com) (free, in the browser, keyboard recommended)  
  
Credits: ithappy (Zombies Mini, Sci-Fi Weapons Mini, Apocalypse FREE, Military FREE), CGPitbull (A-20 Thunderbolt), Eldamar Studio (props).

comments.author: HallucinatedGames
comments.body: I found this to be a fun little game! Tell the dude to keep it up. There's good mechanics and tension between running around the city streets, fending off the zombies, and getting boxed in.

replies.author: YouCantGoThat_Way
replies.body: Thank you! I read this to him and he's thrilled. Can I ask how far you got, and was there a moment where it felt too hard or unfair? He's trying to decide whether to make level 1 easier.

replies.author: HallucinatedGames
replies.body: I almost beat first level. I played maybe 10 minutes. I think of you level up a bit faster to adjust. Collecting coins is good but it takes a little too long to level up in my opinion. Also it was unclear I needed to stay around for 3 waves to rescue the survivors - maybe a little more screen guidance. Keep building!

comments.author: NimbusFPV
comments.body:
This is a really cool game, and great work! The models, graphics, sound, and most of the UI are excellent.

**Rescue zone clarity**  
Others have mentioned it isn’t obvious that you need to stay in the pickup area for three waves to get survivors. I got confused when the game said there were 6 zombies left, but they never came to the chopper. When I walked out of the zone, it told me to get back to the chopper. A more prominent rescue circle would help, along with a countdown timer that warns you when you’re outside it and need to get back in.  I wasn't sure if I was supposed to wait for them to come to me or I needed to go find them. 

**Navigation**  
The arrow pointing over the fence toward the house made me think I should head there instead of staying in the landing zone. The pink arrow is also hard to read. It wasn’t clear what it wanted me to do. It could update its direction more often and  indicate to the player to hold position when needed.

**Shooting**  
I think a point-and-click or tap shooting mechanic would be more engaging than the current auto-aim. Auto-aim sometimes targets cars and vehicles instead of zombies. When you’re running from a train of zombies, it’s frustrating when your gun fires at one far off while a closer zombie gets ignored, or when you start shooting a parked car instead.

**Explosive barrels**  
The barrels explode automatically when player collides, which makes it hard to move through the map without taking damage. Being able to shoot them on purpose to take out zombies would be a fun addition.

**Difficulty and pacing**  
The zombies are intense. They’re fast, and there’s not much room to get away. Giving the player a bit more speed (maybe limited sprinting) or more freedom to move around map would make it easier to escape.

**Dead ends**  
I got stuck a few times on dead-end streets without enough space or firepower to get away.

Overall, very cool and great work!

replies.author: YouCantGoThat_Way
replies.body:
Thank you so much for taking the time to write all of this. It's the most detailed feedback we've gotten, and almost everything you pointed out was something we hadn't noticed ourselves.

We went through your list and most of it is in the game now. Rescues have a big glowing circle around the landing zone, the game tells you to hold the zone for three waves, and if you step outside you get a countdown to get back in. Zombies that wander off or get stuck no longer hold up the wave, so you shouldn't be stuck waiting on six that never show. The arrow at the top follows the road now instead of pointing over fences, and during a rescue it switches to HOLD.

The gun also shoots the closest zombies first, including the ones right behind you, and it stops wasting shots on cars when zombies are around. Barrels don't go off when you walk past anymore. You can shoot them, grenades and mines set them off, and they chain into each other. If a group of zombies bunches up next to one while you're clear, the gun takes the shot for you.

Sprinting and the dead ends are still on the list. Until then, if you'd rather aim yourself, there's a mouse aim option in the Esc menu.

If you give it another try, we'd love to hear how it feels. And thanks again for being so kind about it. My son was really excited about it.

comments.author: Timely-Tradition-471
comments.body:
Raptor vs. zombies is already a pretty great game concept, but I love that your son is actually playing each build and giving specific feedback on what needs to change. Those little comments about the helicopter and the muzzle flash are great. It's also cool that he's involved in shaping the game rather than just watching it come together.

I'm Josh, by the way. I recently joined the Tripo Studio team here in the U.S. and enjoy connecting with people building creative projects like this. I'd love to see how Jurassic Rampage develops. How has the Tripo-to-Mixamo workflow been working for the Brute boss? Would be great to hear what your son thinks of the final result!
